intent: Change one thing from iteration 3: wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m. Keep the 16 mm sensors, the 0.16 m spread, the y = 0.07 m lead, and the 25-times-x weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the Integrator needs no gain change. Expected result: oval progress rises above 0.1175 and max_error falls below 0.06, because the narrower track gives more turn authority for corrections. Keep the s-bend and slalom progress at or above their iteration 3 levels. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 on the s-bend with completion still zero, the narrower track is over-responding and the next step is wheel_track 0.12 with a lower lead (y = 0.06), not a further narrowing.
learning: Hypothesis A (turn authority): with wheel_track 0.10 m, oval max_error falls below 0.06 and oval progress rises above 0.1175. This would confirm that turn response, not sensor position, limits the oval. Hypothesis B (over-response): the narrower track raises s-bend and slalom steering_oscillation above the iteration 3 values (0.144 and 0.153) without a progress gain. If A holds, next test the lead at y = 0.08. If B holds, go back to 0.12 and test y = 0.08 with the gains left alone.
rationale: Iteration 3 (16 mm sensors, y = 0.07 m, 0.16 m spread) is the best result so far at 54.90, up from 26.64. The gain came from the s-bend (progress 0.04 to 0.165) and the slalom (0.03 to 0.1075), and the oval line losses stayed at zero. Oval progress did not move, though: 0.115 in iteration 2, 0.1175 in iteration 3. max_error sits at the 0.06 m off-track floor on every track, and the floor cannot be raised by body width, because even at 0.18 m the limit is only 0.0575 m. The Integrator's pre-race feedback set a rule for this case: if oval progress stays flat near 0.115 with max_error still about 0.06 at y = 0.07, test wheel_track 0.10. That condition now holds. Oval steering_oscillation is 0.074, well below the 0.10 limit that would call for pulling the lead back, so the forward lead is not causing jitter there. The s-bend oscillation did rise to 0.144, which I will watch but do not treat as a reason to revert. Narrowing the track to 0.10 m, with mass and sensors unchanged, raises turn rate per unit of wheel-speed difference (turn rate = wheel speed difference / wheel_track), so the robot can correct harder at the same controller output. Sensor geometry and the 25-per-metre weights stay fixed, so this race isolates turn authority.
